root_cause.text: In fuse_add_dirent_to_cache(), the code fails to validate that the serialized dirent size (reclen) does not exceed PAGE_SIZE before copying it into a page-cache page, allowing a malicious FUSE server to specify a large namelen that causes a buffer overflow during memcpy().
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (reclen > PAGE_SIZE) return;` to reject oversized dirents. The commit message explains that the existing logic only checks remaining space in the current page but never whether the record itself exceeds PAGE_SIZE, and that a namelen of 4095 produces a 4120-byte record that overflows a 4 KiB page by 24 bytes.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement calculates the serialized dirent size (reclen) without any upper bound check against PAGE_SIZE, allowing a malicious server to set a large namelen.
This memcpy copies the dirent into the page-cache page using the attacker-controlled reclen, causing a buffer overflow when reclen exceeds the remaining space in the page.
Declaration of reclen variable without initialization or subsequent validation, used in the vulnerable memcpy.
Maps the page-cache page into kernel address space; the destination of the overflow is this mapping.
Unmaps the page after the copy; the overflow has already occurred, corrupting adjacent kernel data.
